description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of datasets over time, categorized by researcher location, from 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents “Year,” with categories listed in ascending order from 2012 to 2022, while the vertical axis represents “Number of datasets” on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^0 to 10^2.  For each year, there are grouped bars representing the number of datasets from different locations: “Other” (light blue), “USA” (orange), “UK” (red), “IN” (green), “IT” (purple), and “DE” (brown). In 2012, the “USA” bar is approximately 20 datasets, while the “Other” bar is approximately 1 dataset. In 2022, the “USA” bar reaches approximately 80 datasets, and the “Other” bar is approximately 10 datasets. The bars are not explicitly sorted, and no bars are visually emphasized.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of datasets over time for the five most frequent researcher locations and all other locations combined, spanning the years 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the years, while the vertical axis indicates the number of datasets on an exponential scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^2. Researchers from the USA consistently published the highest number of datasets across all years, with a peak in 2020. Notably, researchers from India surpassed those from the UK in dataset production in 2021, marking a significant shift in contributions. Additionally, the number of datasets from Germany declined steadily after 2018, indicating reduced activity in dataset production from this region.
